items.stem: What is the primary purpose of a work-in-progress (WIP) limit?

options.text: To improve flow by reducing multitasking and exposing bottlenecks
options.rationale: Correct: limiting WIP shortens lead time and surfaces constraints.

options.text: To cap how many people can be on the team
options.rationale: WIP limits constrain concurrent work items, not headcount.

options.text: To guarantee every task is finished the same day
options.rationale: WIP limits improve flow but do not fix delivery times.

options.text: To stop the team from ever starting new work
options.rationale: They regulate, not prohibit, starting work.

items.explanation: Correct: limiting WIP shortens lead time and surfaces constraints.

items.stem: Which TWO metrics directly describe the flow of work through a Kanban system? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: lead time measures how long work takes from request to done.
Correct: throughput measures items completed per period.
Headcount is a resource, not a flow metric.
Output volume of docs is not a flow metric.

items.explanation: Correct: lead time and throughput are core flow metrics.

options.text: Address the review bottleneck before starting more work
options.rationale: Correct: relieving the constraint improves overall flow.

options.text: Add more columns to the board
options.rationale: More columns do not clear the bottleneck.
Deleting a needed step trades flow for quality risk.
